summary: cro checked in 3 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: CRO handoff: retain execution-integrity control-plane work as a deferred product specification, not an implementation admission. Evidence: 108 approved proposals lack execution, 164 work items are stranded, 10/10 delivery slots are occupied, 21 requests failed, and approved-proposal execution is 63%. Fleet use case: one canonical opportunity-to-request record with overlap detection, stale-work escalation, and explicit blocked/closed states. Expected metric: higher approved-proposal execution rate, fewer stranded items and failed repairs, lower cycle time. Smallest reversible prototype: read-only reconciliation view over existing proposal, request, work-item, site-overlap, and slot fields. No new telemetry, scheduling, deployment, or spend while containment remains active.

CRO handoff: retain AI-usage cancellation and cost-guardrail work as a deferred control-plane specification. Evidence: 5,316 AI calls, 229 errors, $950.44 recorded cost, uneven site spend, and saturated delivery. Fleet use case: cancel stale or superseded runs, suppress duplicate retries, and expose cost/error state on existing work records. Expected metric: fewer avoidable calls and failed retries without reducing verified delivery throughput. Smallest reversible prototype: read-only stale-run and duplicate-retry report using existing AI-usage, request, and outcome fields. No schedule changes, credentials, spend, dependencies, or deployment while containment remains active.

CRO handoff: keep microsoft/markitdown research-only and do not queue a prototype this cycle. Validation evidence: the bounded lab run passed 8/8 checks, found a MIT license, 194 files, and 22 purpose-specific SEO/content capability hits; dependency installation and production access were not used. Fleet use case: convert approved source documents into structured Markdown for draft content and SEO discovery workflows. Risks: transitive dependency and parser security review, maintenance/release drift, source-rights and derivative-content review, and possible extraction errors. Expected metric: prototype conversion success and editor acceptance rate, with no revenue or ranking claim. Smallest reversible prototype: disposable-workspace conversion of a tiny owner-approved fixture set with provenance, diff review, and deletion after evaluation. CTO/security/legal review remains required before adoption.
